taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Bori-police-station, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 150 | 1.23 | 1.23
2 | 97.1 | 6.21 | 7.44
3 | 284 | 37.5 | 45
4 | 700 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Bori-police-station, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Bori-Police-Station, Bori Metropolis**

The interpreted VES model at this station comprises four layers. Layer 1 (150 Ω·m, 1.23 m thick) overlies Layer 2 (97.1 Ω·m, 6.21 m thick, base at 7.44 m), followed by Layer 3 (284 Ω·m, 37.5 m thick, base at 45 m), and a resistive basal Layer 4 (700 Ω·m, unterminated).

Applying standard curve-type notation: for layers 1-2-3, resistivity decreases then increases (150 > 97.1 < 284), giving an H branch. For layers 2-3-4, resistivity increases steadily (97.1 < 284 < 700), giving an A branch. The correct curve designation is therefore **HA**, not HK as stated in the file. The on-file HK label does not match the actual resistivity sequence, since no K-type inflection (rise then fall) occurs between layers 2-3-4.

Recommend correcting the station record to HA-type prior to finalizing the groundwater interpretation.

{"curve_type_stated": "HA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
